title: Simple F∞ overgroups of groups with decidable word problem
main_claim: Every finitely generated group with decidable word problem embeds in a nontrivial simple group of type F_∞ (higher-finiteness Boone–Higman). Route: build a finitely presented F_2-algebra B (self-referential Kleene fixed point plus the companion's bounded compiler); get a highly transitive action of the ascending torus Λ of δ: E_7(B)→E_7(B) on S = lim B^7; prove every pointwise stabilizer is an ascending torus satisfying a new F_∞ criterion (factorization through St_6(B) plus two commuting-idempotent systems over F_2 and F_3); then apply Belk–Zaremsky twisted Brin–Thompson.

issues.location: Sec. 3 (encoding), Lemma bounded-action-calculus, paragraph 'Substitution with unequal costs'
issues.description: The argument that tested equality in the truncated M(W,Y) code family respects substitution when two tested-equal subwords have different costs is very terse. It relies on 'minimum represented cost' labels and an abstract-word confluence argument. I found no failing step, but this is the least detailed link in the self-referential bootstrap.
issues.evidence: The proof assigns each label its minimum cost in the truncated system and asserts that reductions do not increase total minimum cost. It then asserts that both contextual routes reach the same abstract normal form within budget 2d ≤ 3d. Each step is plausible but is not written out.

issues.location: Lemma compiler (companion Lemma 7.1) and Theorem stage-kernel (companion Theorem 4.1)
issues.description: The main proof depends on two results from the companion paper that were not audited here: the bounded compiler and Steinberg-kernel annihilation. I checked that the statements cited in this paper match the companion's statements word for word in their hypotheses.
issues.evidence: Companion build/bootstrap.tex Lemma 7.1 and build/kernel.tex Theorem 4.1 have the same hypotheses: an additive multiplicative ψ, U_i, V_i in PRP centralizing ψ(R), and V_iU_j = δ_ij P with U_0V_0 + U_1V_1 = P. Here these are instantiated with φ, s_i, d_i from Theorem ring-data(i).

coverage: I read all sections in full. Homological section, checked step by step: Lemma idempotents, including the rank-one exchange identity uλ+vμ=(u+v)λ+v(μ−λ), the F_2 case and the overlap argument; finite presentation of T(U,f) by interleaving; the product-module (Bieri–Eckmann) criterion; Lemma controlled-additivity (AW diagonal, shuffle, the homotopy H⊗F+F'⊗H, and the commuting-image product map with bound control); Prop uniform-fillings induction; the HNN tree, the sequence and local nilpotence of F with (ZJ)^I coefficients; the finite-extension lemma. Stage section, checked by hand: Lemma diagonal (w(v)w(−1), τ_v involutions, the c=c^2 split); injectivity and equivariance of μ and β; the finite-permutation unit v; faithfulness and high transitivity; the stabilizer as ascending torus (t'=ta^{-1}); h_{ℓ,E} landing in U; the exchange matrix E=[[c,d],[−d,c]] with E D_1(v')E^{-1}=D_2(v') using dr=rd=r and dφ²(S_{z_j})=0; f=b∘α through St_6(B). Encoding section: checked the logic of the length-induction bootstrap (3⌊n/10⌋<n, stability, local confluence), the raw-difference embedding i(h)=c(h)−c(ζ), and φ(b)=iκ(b⊗q) with centralizing s_i,d_i. I also checked that the cited companion statements (Lemma 6.4, Lemma 7.1, Theorem 4.1) match. External results were not re-proved: Krstić–McCool (St_n(R) finitely presented for f.p. R, n≥4), Belk–Zaremsky Theorems 3.4 and D, and the companion's proofs.
sibling_notes: The family-250 board was empty when I started. The companion preprint is Finite-algebraic-envelopes-and-the-Boone-Higman-conjecture-September-23-2026. This paper's correctness depends on that companion's Lemma 7.1 (bounded compiler), Lemma 6.4 (binary tail corner, which I checked and which is fine) and Theorem 4.1 (Steinberg kernel annihilation). Whoever audits the companion should look closely at Theorem 4.1 and the compiler's bounded contextual conclusion.
